attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, published under his name and endorsed.

semantics.note: The prediction of unreliability is hedged ('likely'), but the consequence is firm: 'in which case it will' get comparatively little traction. Treating the unreliability as the antecedent keeps the condition and is faithful to his words. No horizon is stated.

contract.note: The contract rightly says 'comparatively little' has no stated baseline, so any comparison would have to be invented. It also rightly says the antecedent is undefined: neither 'unreliable' nor 'adequate augmentation' is given a meaning. Calling the claim not testable as written is fair to the speaker.

evidence.note: A genuine preprint, v3 dated 2026-08-06, before the evaluation date. It finds test-time scaling fails to help on closed-book knowledge tasks. That bears on reliability in one domain but does not establish the antecedent as worded.

A company disclosure by OpenRouter/a16z, available 2025-12-04. Reasoning models' token share on one platform rose above half. That shows uptake, but it is a single platform's token share with no baseline, so it cannot contradict the consequent.

reviews.rationale: This conditional forecast cannot be scored. Whether the antecedent holds is unknown: e1 shows weakness only on knowledge-intensive tasks, not unreliability across domains where augmentation is inadequate. The consequent has no comparison baseline. e2's sizeable usage share is suggestive counterevidence, but it does not meet an undefined test. Under the policy, a conditional whose antecedent is unknown is not scored.
